beats.text: Install the tool with one command.
Run it and see the first output.
Clone a git repo.
List the files inside.
Start the dev server.
A build fails with a red error.
The fix is a one-line change and the build passes.
Check the disk space with df.
A user asks an assistant how to save money.
The assistant gives three short tips.
Two friends argue about pizza toppings.
One of them gives in.
A customer reports a late parcel.
Support apologises and offers a refund.
The customer says thanks.
An old lighthouse at dawn.
A small boat heads out to sea.
A busy market street.
A vendor smiles at the camera.
The sun sets behind the stalls.
A mountain trail in the fog.
A web page titled Daily News loads.
Its headline and first paragraph appear.
A shop page opens with a product heading.
The price and a Buy button text show up.
Start with the list 5, 2, 9, 1.
Compare the first two numbers and swap them.
Mark the sorted cells as done.
Binary search for 7 in the sorted list 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
Highlight the middle cell and move the pointer right.
Quiz: which planet is closest to the Sun?
Reveal the answer after a pause.
Quiz: what does HTTP stand for? Give three options.
Reveal the correct option.
Footage of waves rolling onto a beach, with a short caption.
Hold on the shot.
A time-lapse of city traffic at night.
Caption it: rush hour.
A laptop sends a message to a cloud.
A lock appears over the cloud.
A light bulb appears for an idea.
A rocket launches below it.
A DNS lookup: your browser asks a resolver for example.com.
The resolver asks a root server, then returns the address.
A phone sends a request to a server through a router.
The server sends the page back.
Solve 2x + 6 = 14.
Subtract 6 from both sides.
Divide by 2 to get x = 4.
Expand (a + b)^2.
The result is a^2 + 2ab + b^2.
Flip a fair coin 20 times.
About half land heads.
Roll a die 30 times and count each face.
Each face shows roughly a sixth of the time.
A sheet lists three products with their prices.
Add a SUM formula for the total and highlight it.
A budget table with Month and Spend columns.
Highlight the biggest month.
A bar chart of sales for Q1 to Q4.
Q4 is the highest.
A pie chart of where a budget goes: rent, food, fun.
Rent is the biggest slice.
Three photos of a trip appear one after another.
Show them in a grid.
A hero photo of a mountain with a strip of smaller shots below.
Each gets a short caption.
A chess puzzle: white to move and mate in two.
Play the queen to h7, then explain the follow-up.
The Italian opening: e4 e5, Nf3 Nc6, Bc4.
Arrows show the bishop aiming at f7.
Play a C major chord on the piano.
Then an F major chord.
Play the first notes of Twinkle Twinkle: C C G G A A G.
Label the key as C major.
A map of Europe with three cities: Paris, Berlin and Rome.
Draw a route through them in order.
Mark Tokyo and Sydney on a world map.
Add a title: two big hubs.
The planets orbit the Sun.
Inner planets move faster than outer ones.
The Moon circles the Earth once a month.
Show them as a small orbit.
